articles.title: One of 2028's Biggest Upcoming Games Reportedly Coming to Nintendo Switch 2
articles.summary: One of 2028's biggest upcoming games — currently only confirmed for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X — is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 when it releases. This has not been confirmed, but it may have just been leaked. The new leak comes from Amazon, and specifically, Amazon News, and has since been deleted by […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of 2028's biggest upcoming games — currently only confirmed for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X — is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 when it releases. This has not been confirmed, but it may have just been leaked. The new leak comes from Amazon, and specifically, Amazon News, and has since been deleted by Amazon, but not before the Internet got its receipt.

Back on December 11, 2025, Tomb Raider: Catalyst was announced at The Game Awards by series developer Crystal Dynamics and Amazon Games. Now, a year later, Amazon News officially noted the game was coming to Nintendo Switch 2, and seems to suggest this version would be available at launch. This could just be an honest error, but the timing is interesting, because The Game Awards are right around the corner, and it would be fitting for the game to reappear with a new trailer and word of a new platform. In other words, this may be less of an honest error and simply letting the beans spill a little early, which happens. Many ports, release dates, and even games themselves have leaked this way in the past.

A Nintendo Switch 2 port for the game seems completely plausible if not likely, but often Nintendo gets ports of games after their launch. If this version is leaking this early, it's reasonable to assume the Nintendo Switch 2 version will be ready at launch. That said, take everything here with a grain of salt. None of this is official information. For what it is worth, neither Crystal Dynamics nor Amazon Games have commented on the potential leak. If it were fake, they could have just shut it down, but to be fair, many game developers and publishers have a universal policy of silence when it comes to rumors, leaks, and specualtion.

The 14th Tomb Raider Game For those who do not know what Tomb Raider: Catalyst is, it is the 14th installment in the series, at least of the mainline variety. It's not another reboot, though. Rather, it is a sequel to Tomb Raider: Underworld , released in 2008. To this end, the story takes place in Northern India after the events of Underworld , where Lara Croft must navigate the aftermath of a mythical cataclysm. While a sequel to Underworld , the expectation is that the game is going to be made in a way that playing Underworld won't be required. Meanwhile, the new installment looks poised to make a huge change to the series .

Officially, Tomb Raider: Catalyst is in development for PC, PS5, Xbox Series S, and Xbox Series X. Unofficially, it may be coming to Nintendo Switch 2 as well. Whatever the case, it is currently slated for release in 2027.

articles.title: Is Vanity Fair’s Hit Piece on Taylor Swift Really Journalism?
articles.summary: After word hit the street some days back that Vanity Fair was imminently going to publish an extensively reported hit piece on music's biggest superstar, there was some anticipation that Monday might turn out to be a bad day for Taylor Swift. Instead, it was just a bad day for journalism. As attention-seeking magazine articles […]
articles.content:
After word hit the street some days back that Vanity Fair was imminently going to publish an extensively reported hit piece on music's biggest superstar, there was some anticipation that Monday might turn out to be a bad day for Taylor Swift . Instead, it was just a bad day for journalism. As attention-seeking magazine articles go, it's hard to remember one that landed with quite such an unanticipated — but very loud — thud as "The Mastermind," which has even hardened anti-Swifties wondering whether May Jeong slipped it through without editorial oversight, sneaking an alleged year's worth of work onto the internet in the dead of morning.

The alternative scenario was unthinkable. You would have to imagine that the author had actually been encouraged by editors to puzzle readers with a reported op-ed in which the subject of the piece — apparently, some top-tier celebrity! — is never named, yet still is subject to accusations that she picks her own friends, harbors ambitions, owned three pairs of Ugg boots while posing as a teenage commoner, and, most slanderously, was actually popular in school.

When was the last time a high-profile magazine piece got ratio-ed this badly? That would have been one year and one week ago, when an exclusive excerpt from Olivia Nuzzi's memoir, "American Canto," was released to an incredulous world. And if there's something that feels a little bit familiar about Jeong's oddball tactic of not naming names in her piece (or at least not the big ones), it's because this "you know who it's about, but we're not gonna say anyway" technique was a weird conceit last grafted into big-time American journalism by Nuzzi. That author referred to RFK only as "the Politician," her ex-boyfriend as "the man I did not marry," and so on. Nuzzi walked so that Jeong could run. Although this new piece is not any kind of roman a clef, she still feels compelled to euphemize Swift as "The Star," her former label as "The Machine," Scooter Braun as "The Manager," Charli xcx as "The Brat" and even a secondary source as "The Person Familiar."

You would think Vanity Fair's editors would recall the horrible reviews Nuzzi got for employing this gambit in "American Canto," especially since the excerpt that introduced that annoying running gag to the world was published in… Vanity Fair. (How quickly they forget, but monthly journalism is a grind.)

The article aims to unload secrets, but the secret we really need revealed is: Why do that? An interview with Jeoing is in order. Or perhaps she is saving the rationale for her journalism class at Princeton, which may be the only one destined to have "The Mastermind" as ciriculum. On first blush, a journalism non-pro might imagine that it was done to skirt libel laws, although that explanation holds no water, since the writer does quote several of her lowest-level sources by name, like the kids from Swift's school who are ready to call her out now for not having been friendless or unmoneyed. (The former classmates will pick up some notoriety now, but will they regret that they could have become even more legendary if they'd been ID-ed as "The Girl Who Noticed The Star's Uggs"?) No, it seems more likely that Jeong did it because we are, all of us, just archetypes in a fable. Except for the music teacher at Wyomissing Area Junior/Senior High, who is un-archetypical enough to require a first and last name. Related Stories Cannes Condemns Five-Year Prison Sentence Against Iranian Palme d’Or Winner Jafar Panahi and Pleads for International Support

Or perhaps Jeong refrains from naming Swift because she is the female equivalent of two other characters who are often referred to as He Who Must Not Be Named: Voldemort and Trump. Certainly the article seems to see Swift as an exemplor of the banality of evil, or, more to the point, a modern-day, real-life Regina George from "Mean Girls." (No, not making that up, the journalist really goes with that.) Nearly every sentence is intended as a slap. Most journos writing a piece remotely in this vein — a reported one, as opposed to a straight opinion — would try to leaven it at least once or twice with a positive or just neutral observation, before dropping the next bomb. "The Mastermind," to its honest credit, dispenses with any "See, I went into this with an open mind" niceties. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The Star is found to be "making herself a metonym for all women, successfully equat(ing) criticism against her as criticism against womenkind." Compared to Katy Perry (or "The California Girl"), who is "an adult pretending to be a child," Swift "might be a child pretending to be an adult." She "has a reputation for being punitive. She seems too invested in her own victimhood." For Swift, "all she had ever wanted from the world was that it celebrate her milky goodness, that her altruism not be mistaken for covert narcissism." And then from there, Jeoing gets to some of Swift's bad qualities. (Just kidding.)

If this were framed in any way as a commentary, as opposed to Vanity Fair objectively speaking in the voice of God, it wouldn't catch much notice. But instead, the magazine frames it as an ultimate profile, the result of a year of work and talking to "over 100 sources." We have to take the editors' word for that, because the reportage, as printed, only quotes six sources on the record: the mother of a man who directed Swift in her school plays, a guitar teacher, a school music teacher, two girls who sat near Swift in music class, and a poet who is called in to assess how lyrics work. Five others are quoted anonymously: someone who used to be close to Swift called The Person Familiar; a music pro called The Exec; a mystery collaborator with a profession that must be kept secret; a musician who toured with Swift; and a critic who was ostracized after slamming her. Now, reporters do often get great background information from interviews they don't quote, so the 100-plus figure doesn't sound unrealistic. But if these dozen or so sources were the best that the story had to actually quote — including a poet and a critic — you do have to wonder who the other 85-plus were, to be less quotable. (An editor's introduction to the piece says one of the people interviewed was a "lover" of Swift's, but we'll just have to guess if the writer got to Joe Alwyn.) blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

All that said, there are a handful of interesting questions and critical observations scattered through Jeong's piece. (See? This is the part where you throw in something nice, to show you were objective.) If you removed the promise of fact-finding and this existed as an essay on Salon — RIP — you could credit her with some food-for-thought lines and decently snarky zingers. (Sure, I chuckled when Jeong, alluding to Travis Kelce, wrote, "Regretfully we must call him Redwood.")

But the veneer of investigative reporting placed upon this piece mostly shows just how low the bar is for an attempted expose anymore. Even without the terminally cutesy names. It'd be nice to suppose that Jeong really did come up with something after a year — there is so much hinted at that is quickly dropped — and that Vanity Fair's lawyers gutted the piece to within an inch of a life. But more probably it's an example of snark masquerading as reportage. And it's a lesson that some journalists (even journalists that teach at Princeton) are too quick to succumb to a sad maxim, when an expensive and exhaustive fishing expedition doesn't turn up much: If you can't get the goods, just get cute. But don't expect readers who expect more out of their hit squads not to notice.

articles.title: Jason Sudeikis And Olivia Wilde Had A 'Complicated' Split, But He Does Credit Her For Ted Lasso
articles.summary: The exes seem more amicable than ever.
articles.content:
Remember when Olivia Wilde was served child custody papers by Jason Sudeikis while she was on stage in front of thousands presenting Don’t Worry Darling at CinemaCon ? That was over four years ago in the heat of the pair figuring out the post-split situation . However, these days, the two seem to be on better terms. To that point, Sudeikis is even crediting his ex for the creation of his massively successful TV show, Ted Lasso (which just got big news by the way).

As Sudeikis shared during an interview at a special live edition of the show at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles, Wilde was the person who actually followed up with her then-partner on the Ted Lasso idea years before him and the other creators knew what to do with the character. As Sudeikis continued:

Wild, right? Mr. Ted Lasso himself, alongside two of his co-creators Brendan Hunt, Joe Kelly, sat on the idea for a while until one day they were overflowing with ideas. And then, they sat on it again until this happened. In Sudeikis’ words:

Now that Ted Lasso is one of the best shows to watch with an Apple TV subscription , it’s pretty crazy to think how long the whole process took. It took so long that when the idea was first formed Sudeikis and Wilde went from being an engaged couple to splitting up . Thankfully it did, because it’s one of my favorite shows on streaming in recent years.

articles.title: Bela Bajaria Calls Time at Netflix a "Fun Chapter" as She Teases Rest and "Conversations" in First Remarks Since Exit
articles.summary: The former chief content officer at the streaming service was ousted last month, with Peter Rice taking over her role.
articles.content:
Former Netflix chief content officer Bela Bajaria addressed her exit from the streamer in her first public comments since her abrupt departure last month.

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter ahead of the 2026 International Emmys , where she's set to be honored with the Founders Award , Bajaria called her decade at Netflix "such an amazing, fun chapter" and shared she was "proud of so many of the things" that she and her team had accomplished.

Since her exit, Bajaria said she's been indulging in "a little rest" and having some "really fun conversations." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Sadie Sandler to Star in Netflix Horror Movie 'Malibu' From Vertigo, Happy Madison (Exclusive) Movies 'The Odyssey' Leads Critics Choice Awards Below-The-Line Shortlists

"I'm excited about what's next, and I think this time is good for a little rest after a lot of global travel," she told THR on the red carpet ahead of the awards show, adding that she's "really open" to whatever the future holds.

Bajaria was ousted from her role at Netflix on Oct. 15, with former Fox and Disney exec Peter Rice taking her place as chief content officer.

Bajaria, who joined Netflix after serving as president of Universal Television at NBCUniversal, left the streamer as it shed 1,000 employees, roughly six percent of its workforce, including execs Doug Belgrad and, days after news broke of Bajaria leaving, film boss Dan Lin. The layoffs came as the company seeks a reset amid slowing viewership growth.

When she left Netflix, co-CEO Ted Sarandos said of Bajaria, “Bela has built and shaped a truly global Content organization, hiring brilliant people and empowering them to make good decisions. I am incredibly grateful to her for everything she’s done."

He added in a staff memo, "I know this is a big change in a year that has already had its share. But I also see an opportunity to take our slate to the next level, especially in [the U.S. and Canada] where we have an outsize impact in creating big, buzzy hits that our members love and drive conversation around the world.”

articles.title: 'GTA 6' Boss Strauss Zelnick Among First Raft of SXSW London 2027 Speakers
articles.summary: The upcoming installment — built around the theme "The Power of Human Potential" — has also enlisted former DeepMind creative lead Jon Steinback and president of Genomics Limited David Thornton.
articles.content:
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick, the man behind Grand Theft Auto VI , is among the first raft of speakers confirmed for next year's SXSW London .

The conference is set to return to Shoreditch, east London, for its third year from May 24-29, where Zelnick will take to the stage to talk about building one of the world's biggest entertainment franchises (sales for the latest release have already out-grossed Christopher Nolan's box office behemoth The Odyssey ).

The upcoming installment is built around the theme "The Power of Human Potential," described by organizers as a deliberate focus on people in a year dominated by what machines can do. Among the speakers making that case is Jon Steinback, the former DeepMind creative lead whose start-up Marker is building an AI writing tool designed to develop, rather than delete, writers. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies How Iran's Pegah Ahangarani Turned Her Family Archives Into a Regime-Challenging Oscar Hopeful Music Don Toliver Postpones O2 Arena Show After Evacuation Due to "Unknown Substance" Released at Manchester Concert

Elsewhere, David Thornton, president of Genomics Limited, will explore how rapid analysis of large-scale genetic and genomic information will empower us to predict disease risks and improve medicine.

Ilyas Khan, who founded Cambridge Quantum and was the founding CEO of Quantinuum, is also on board to discuss the convergence of AI and quantum computing. His appearance follows Quantinuum’s $1.68bn Nasdaq listing in June 2026, the largest traditional IPO yet for a pure-play quantum computing company.

Two of Britain’s best-known voices in advertising, Martin Sorrell and Rory Sutherland, and media personality GK Barry, will join the festival to explore the future of advertising and the creator economy, while Refik Anadol, founder of the newly opened LA museum, Dataland, will share his artistic vision for AI and data-driven installations. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"SXSW London is a place of firsts — where you see it first, hear it first, and meet the people behind it first," began Katy Arnander, SXSW London's chief programming officer. "It's also where industries converge: where gaming meets advertising, art meets AI, and quantum computing shares a stage with the creator economy. Our first wave of speakers reflects exactly that, and shows what happens when human potential is central to the conversation."

The event will welcome around 20,000 festival-goers on its walkable Shoreditch campus, engaging in networking, music showcases, international premieres and parties. The 2026 festival drew attendees from 97 countries, 863 speakers (including Michelle Obama, Serena Williams and Brian Eno), 256 music artists across 18 venues and 100 film screenings, 13 of them world premieres.

articles.title: Netflix Is About to Lose All Five Seasons of a Near-Perfect "Game of Thrones with Vikings" Series but You Still Have Time to Binge-Watch It
articles.summary: Courtesy of Netflix/Carnival Films & Television Everyone loves a big action-packed historical TV series and one show that could give Game of Thrones a run for its money is one of the best out there. However, the series that launched in 2015 and ran for five seasons and a wrap-up movie is about to become much harder to watch in the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Everyone loves a big action-packed historical TV series and one show that could give Game of Thrones a run for its money is one of the best out there. However, the series that launched in 2015 and ran for five seasons and a wrap-up movie is about to become much harder to watch in the U.S. as all episodes will be leaving its home on Netflix in less than a month. Yet all is not lost as you could easily binge the 46 episodes of The Last Kingdom before December 9 to see why this show has a massive 95% Popcornmeter rating on Rotten Tomatoes. The series' departure from Netflix has come as a surprise to fans, who assumed that as Netflix is co-producer they would be keeping the show on their platform permanently. However, with the show originally airing on BBC America before Netflix became involved it seems that pesky licensing rules are shipping it off the platform.

The Last Kingdom earned rave reviews from its first episodes and, unlike Game of Thrones , continued to please viewers through until its final episode. Based on the novels of Bernard Cornwell's The Saxon Stories series, the show is packed with brutal and bloody battles, political manipulation, and the kind of drama that made George R.R. Martin's fantasy epic such a hit on HBO. However, The Last Kingdom has its story rooted in real history. Even though Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire bases several aspects of its story in historical places and events, such as The Wall being a representation of Hadrian's Wall in northern England, and the battle of the Starks and Lannisters drawing inspiration from the War of the Roses between the houses of Lancaster and York, Cornwell's work is truer to the kind of power struggles that actually took place in England.

The Last Kingdom tells of the bloody struggle to reunite England during the ninth and 10th centuries. Dane raised Saxon Uhtred of Bebbanburg, played by Alexander Dreymon, is the central conflicted character of the saga, who fights to reclaim his ancestral home while struggling to work out which side he should actually be fighting for. Across five seasons, Uhtred's path is one that brings him into several intense conflicts, puts his loyalties to the test, and provides a thrilling story that kept both audiences and critics watching the show to its conclusion. Before the end of the series in 2022, a sequel feature length movie was announced under the title of The Last Kingdom: Seven Kings Must Die . The movie debuted on Netflix in 2023 to conclude the story.

The biggest achievement of The Last Kingdom was being able to maintain its high standard throughout the entire series. Game of Thrones proved how hard it can be to deliver a satisfying conclusion to a long-running series, but one thing the show had going for it was that all of its books were available at the time it reached the end. Where HBO's series needed to go beyond Martin's books in order to complete the tale, The Last Kingdom clearly benefited from having everything laid out ready in advance. That means that even if you have already seen it, The Last Kingdom is a series that is always worth a rewatch . If you live in the U.S., then you have until December 9 to get in on the action, which those in the U.K., Europe, and other territories, the series is set to remain with the streamer until 2028. The Last Kingdom: Seven Kings Must Die will not be leaving Netflix and will remain on the platform worldwide.

Have you see The Last Kingdom ? Is it better than Game of Thrones ? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Unannounced Doomsday Hero Has Been Hiding Their Casting in Plain Sight for Weeks, According to MCU Theory & The Reveal Will Be Amazing
articles.summary: Marvel fans think they've figured out how the studio plans to announce Iman Vellani's return as Ms. Marvel in Avengers: Doomsday. The actress has spent the last few months co-hosting Marvel's Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday podcast with Frank Alvarez. While Vellani's involvement in the movie has yet to be confirmed, the recent announcement that Hailee […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel fans think they've figured out how the studio plans to announce Iman Vellani's return as Ms. Marvel in Avengers: Doomsday . The actress has spent the last few months co-hosting Marvel's Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday podcast with Frank Alvarez. While Vellani's involvement in the movie has yet to be confirmed, the recent announcement that Hailee Steinfeld will return as Kate Bishop has fans taking a closer look at the podcast's set. Specifically, they're looking at Vellani's chair.

Marvel Studios has managed to turn a piece of furniture into one of the most effective marketing tools in Hollywood. Since the hours-long livestream announcing the cast of Avengers: Doomsday , getting a chair has become a rite of passage for actors joining the movie. When Steinfeld received her chair while promoting Disney's Hexed , fans realized Vellani had been sitting in a similar director's chair since the podcast debuted in August. Fans on Reddit are now speculating that Marvel is saving the reveal of what's on the back of Vellani's chair for the final episode of the podcast.

Me, conspicuously eyeing the Iman Vellani chair on the Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday podcast. https://t.co/tjk5ozutHj pic.twitter.com/63PeuHFBCb

If Marvel wanted to sneak another casting announcement past fans, Vellani would be the perfect accomplice. The actress is arguably as big a Marvel fan as anyone watching the podcast. Getting to spend a few months talking about the MCU without letting slip that she's in the next Avengers movie seems like something Vellani would have a lot of fun with. This isn't the first time someone has potentially let slip that Vellani is in the movie, either. Earlier this year, Andy Serkis told Vellani he was excited to see her in Avengers: Doomsday . Whether Serkis knew something we didn't or was simply having some fun with the actress remains to be seen.

When we last saw Kamala Khan, she was doing her best Nick Fury impression. The post-credits scene of The Marvels saw Kamala show up at Kate Bishop's apartment to recruit the young archer. She even mentioned that Ant-Man had a daughter. Three years later, Marvel has confirmed that both Steinfeld and Kathryn Newton will appear in Avengers: Doomsday , but not the actress whose character was responsible for getting the team together in the first place. Adding to the speculation is footage from the ScreenX presentation of an Avengers: Doomsday trailer that appears to place Scott and Cassie Lang inside Kate's apartment. Could we finally be getting a payoff to the scene that closed out The Marvels ?

Vellani's absence from the original cast announcement was particularly surprising given how much of Kamala's story has revolved around her love of the Avengers and a piece of alien tech in her gauntlets. We were introduced to the character in an episode of Ms. Marvel that took her to AvengerCon. Getting to see Kamala interact with some of the heroes she grew up idolizing would be one of the joys of bringing her into an Avengers movie. For all the talk of returning X-Men and Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom, Avengers: Doomsday also has an opportunity to make good on some of the promises Marvel made during the Multiverse Saga. It would be a shame to finally get the Young Avengers together without Kamala. Avengers: Doomsday opens in theaters on December 18th.

articles.title: 5 Marvel Characters Who Are Nothing Like Their Debut Appearances
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Marvel Comics has changed a lot since the company started making superhero comics. However, while most heroes and villains change a lot over the years, they are still recognizable today compared to how they looked when they debuted. No matter how much Hulk has changed, he eventually goes back to how fans recognize him best. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics has changed a lot since the company started making superhero comics. However, while most heroes and villains change a lot over the years, they are still recognizable today compared to how they looked when they debuted. No matter how much Hulk has changed, he eventually goes back to how fans recognize him best. Peter Parker might have grown up, but Spider-Man is still the same wisecracking hero he has always been. Even Magneto, who has been a hero for a very long time now, still has the same basic look and powers that he has had since he debuted in X-Men #1 (1963) so many years ago.

However, there are some heroes who debuted in Marvel Comics, and today they have changed drastically. In some cases, they have been de-aged, and in others they have developed deeper stories that made them so much more than what they originally were. There is also one hero who looks and acts the exact same, but her powers and origin have drastically changed thanks to an MCU streaming series.

Natasha Romanoff debuted in Tales of Suspense #52 (1964) by Stan Lee, Don Rico, and Don Heck. She was a Soviet agent sent to seduce Tony Stark while her partner Boris Turgenov attacked Anton Vanko and stole his armor. She had no costume, no red hair, and never threw a punch. She was infatuated with Stark's looks and wealth and easily distracted by jewelry, and she feared her Soviet superiors more than her enemies. She was a femme fatale who was used to distract and even assassinate wealthy and powerful men.

However, that is not how Black Widow looks or acts today. Once she defected, she eventually joined the Avengers and became a spy and secret agent working for the United States. The black suit and red hair debuted in The Amazing Spider-Man #86 (1970), and she ended up teaming with Daredevil starting in Daredevil #81, which is where her personality began to really change. Later stories rebuilt her origin around the Red Room, which implanted false memories, and that version morphed into the Black Widow fans know today.

Sam Wilson debuted in Captain America #117 (1969) by Stan Lee and Gene Colan. He is an interesting case because he has drastically changed not only in his role as a hero but also in his secret identity role. When Sam debuted, he was a social worker who helped the kids on the streets. He became the Falcon, a sidekick to Captain America, and they shared an interesting dynamic as Cap signified fighting for his country while Falcon was more about helping the people the country often ignored or forgot about.

Sam Wilson became Captain America in Captain America #25 (2014) after Steve Rogers lost the Super Soldier Serum and aged. He is still someone who fights more for the people than for the government. An example is when he fought against the anti-immigrant Sons of the Serpent on the U.S.-Mexico border, a storyline that made real-world news about the issues he faced in the comics. Sam returned to his Falcon role for a short time, but that part of his life is over with, and Sam is now as much Captain America as Steve Rogers is.

When Kamala Khan debuted, she was an Inhuman with the power to stretch and alter her body, similar to that of Plastic Man in DC Comics. She was also a teenager, and while she was a member of the Avengers for a time, she made her name as a leader on the teenage Champions team with Nova and Miles Morales. As a young, teenage Muslim hero, she was fresh and different, and she gave a new generation of fans a hero they could see themselves in.

However, things changed in comics for Kamala. While she is still the teenager who loves her family and has an intense fangirl attitude toward Captain Marvel, Kamala Khan is now a mutant/Inhuman hybrid . Marvel has said it always wanted her to be a mutant but made her an Inhuman because she debuted during a time when Marvel was emphasizing Inhumans over mutants for a period. This change happened after Kamala's death, when she ended up resurrected on Krakoa, with Professor X saying she had the latent X-gene. This also gave her new powers of creating hard light constructs, which debuted in her Disney+ MCU series.

Most fans know the Guardians of the Galaxy from the MCU movies, but that team is nothing like the original Guardians. The Guardians of the Galaxy from the movies debuted in 2008 during the Annihilation: Conquest miniseries . However, the original Guardians of the Galaxy debuted in Marvel Super-Heroes #18 (1968) by Arnold Drake, Gene Colan, and Roy Thomas. The first lineup was Vance Astro, Martinex, Charlie-27, and Yondu, each apparently the last of their kind, uniting against the alien Badoon in the 31st century.

This was also a team that played a big role in Marvel in the 1970s. They appeared in Giant-Size Defenders #5 and The Defenders #26-29 (1975), and they also had run-ins with the Avengers during that era. Tom DeFalco relaunched them in 1990 to capitalize on Star Trek: The Next Generation . In 2008, Marvel reimagined them as a team fighting in cosmic wars, with a lineup including Star-Lord, Rocket Raccoon, Groot, Gamora, Drax, Adam Warlock, Phyla-Vell, and Mantis.

Agatha Harkness debuted in Fantastic Four #94 (1969) by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby. She was a woman who Reed Richards and Sue Richards hired as a child-rearing specialist for their baby Franklin. She was an elderly woman with gray hair, and Ben Grimm often jokingly called her an "old cow." She lived in a creepy old house on Whisper Hill, and she often joked that people thought she was a witch. In actuality, she was a witch. She ended up mentoring the Scarlet Witch and is the one who wiped the twins from Wanda's mind after they disappeared in West Coast Avengers.

That was her downfall as well, since Wanda found and killed her in "Avengers Disassembled," which is where the changes began. She later haunted Wanda as a ghost until Natalya Maximoff sacrificed herself to resurrect he r in Scarlet Witch #14. When Agatha came back, she was no longer an elderly woman and was now much younger, and she continued to clash with Wanda. The change made it easier for the MCU to make its version younger, with the character played by Kathryn Hahn.

Which characters do you think have had the better transformation over the years? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

articles.title: Did Marvel Edit Characters Out of the Avengers: Doomsday Trailer? Marvel Fans Spot Mystery Moments
articles.summary: Marvel Studios Avengers: Doomsday's final trailer was exactly what a lot of Marvel Cinematic Universe fans needed to see: a story that had heart and massive stakes to go along with all the Marvel characters that are going to cross over with one another for the first time, combining over a quarter-century of Marvel movie history into […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday 's final trailer was exactly what a lot of Marvel Cinematic Universe fans needed to see: a story that had heart and massive stakes to go along with all the Marvel characters that are going to cross over with one another for the first time, combining over a quarter-century of Marvel movie history into one film. However, all that new footage from Doomsday is also raising some very important new questions. And the Marvel fandom is putting their detective skills together to find some answers.

One of the biggest things being looked at right now is whether or not Marvel Studios is once again pulling a trick with the Avengers: Doomsday footage being shown in trailers. And, unlike ten years ago when we were all being fooled by the very first teasers for Avengers: Infinity War , now we know how to look at what's being shown to us a little bit closer, and with much more scrutiny.

A lot of MCU fans and bloggers have been dissecting the Avengers: Doomsday footage and picking up on the familiar pattern of scenes that have awkwardly conspicuous spaces left open in the frame. It suggests that digital editing has been used to remove a character (or characters ) from the actual finished shot, or that shots may not be entirely genuine at all.

Some key scenes from the latest trailer that seem odd include the shots of the Fantastic Four meeting with Steve Rogers in the 1950s, and later bringing him to Avengers Tower, all of which seem to be missing a character (or more) in the ensemble. Then there's the callback circular shot of the Avengers and X-Men assembling to battle Doom's Sentinels, where there is also space both in the center of the group and next to Sam Wilson (on his left!) where more characters are likely to appear.

Previous trailers also brought up the pivotal meeting scene between Wakanda and the Fantastic Four and Avengers, which has already revealed more visual effects not seen before, like water being displaced so that Namor and the undersea kingdom of Talokan (who we still don't see in the footage) can presumably join the alliance. So this isn't fan conspiracy: Marvel is changing the Avengers: Doomsday footage right in front of our eyes, just like it has before with so many other films.

Fans started catching on as far back as Spider-Man: Homecoming with its faux trailer scenes of Spider-Man and Iron Man flying/swinging into action together; Avengers: Infinity War was the biggest culprit, with Marvel Studios' digital wizards cooking up an entirely fake "Avengers Assemble" team charge during the Battle of Wakanda, featuring Hulk, who never even appeared again after the opening scenes! By the time Avengers: Endgame 's trailer was released, fans were savvy enough to see many of the "spaces" where missing characters were being hidden, while questioning whether other shots were real at all.

As for who Marvel Studios is hiding: ( POTENTIAL SPOILERS !)

One major fan theory says that it is actually Doom who is being edited out of the scenes between Steve Rogers and the Fantastic Four. It's long been rumored that Fantastic Four: First Steps ' post-credits scene of Doom meeting Franklin Richards will segue into Doom teaming up with Marvel's First Family , under the guise of saving the multiverse, while really scheming to create his own new reality.

Doom would supposedly help the F4 track the source of the multiverse collapse back to Steve and his altered timeline, living with Peggy Carter and his son, and use Steve to recruit the Avengers to pit that team against the X-Men and their world. Marvel would obviously want to hide that story detail because it raises so many other questions and theories they'd rather just let the movie answer for itself (like does Doom use Tony Stark's likeness to manipulate Steve – another secret worth hiding).

Shots like the Avengers and X-Men vs. the Sentinels could be hiding any number of characters . Some good guesses are that Monica Rambeau (Teyonah Parris) is involved in this, as an Earth-616 superhero who has been in the custody of the X-Men since she got portaled to Earth-10005 at the end of The Marvels . Other theories say that Ryan Reynolds' Deadpool and Hugh Jackman's Wolverine are part of this battle, but are being saved as a reveal in the film; some deeper fan theories state that characters like Bob/The Sentry/The Void (Lewis Pullman) will be more pivotal than we think, and will fight alongside his buddy and confidant Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh) when she goes to Earth-10005.

Either way, it's fun to know that Avengers: Doomsday is still holding back some big surprises for fans to discover in the theater. We'll soon find out when it's released on December 18th.

articles.title: I Knew Blade Runner 2099 Reviews Would Praise The Visuals, But I’m Surprised By Critics’ Big Critique
articles.summary: Well, I didn't see this coming.
articles.content:
Blade Runner 2099 has arguably been one of the most anticipated titles on the 2026 TV schedule , and there’s a good reason for that. Not only does it expand upon the classic science-fiction franchise, but it also has two capable leads in Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer (who do plenty of stunt work) . The show debuts later this week, and reviews are finally starting to roll in. Having seen the show in its entirety for myself, I figured there would be high praise for the visuals, but I am surprised by one particular critique amongst critics.

2099 – which, of course, takes place 50 years after 2017’s Blade Runner 2049 – sees Replicants having become the ruling class, while humans are treated like vermin. At the center of the story is Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human trying to escape her circumstances by posing as a Replicant Blade Runner. In the process of doing that, she is partnered with Olwen (Yeoh), a dying Replicant Runner. The story does indeed get dark, but I didn’t have much of an issue with it. As for The Guardian’s Rhik Samadder, though, he says:

Samadder also notably calls the visuals both “impressive” and “oppressive” in a way. However, also mentioning that the series also “plunges us into a far darker world” than the Blade Runner movies ( which don’t directly tie into 2099 ). Likewise, Aaron Pruner of CNET isn’t really a fan of the overly dark setting and aesthetic. In his somewhat mixed review, Pruner praises the show’s execution while also posing this question regarding the bleak vibe:

The darkness doesn’t seem to be deterring everyone, though, as Alison Herman of Variety has glowing thoughts on the show. Aside from praising Hunter Schafer, Herman also admires series creator Silka Luisa’s adherence to this storied continuity birthed by Philip K. Dick:

That’s definitely a big compliment, considering how beloved Ridley Scott ’s original 1982 film is and how much critical praise Denis Villeneuve’s 2049 received . Still, not everyone is impressed. TVLine’s Dave Nemetz finds the sci-fi show to be overly bleak as well. Not only that, but he also isn’t too taken with the visuals like a number of others are:

Although I can’t say I saw these critiques about the show’s vibe coming, I can’t blame others for not caring for its dark nature. To me, this kind of style is just baked into the DNA of the franchise, though I can admit that Blade Runner 2099 does delve into murkier territory at times. I’m curious as to how fans will feel when all eight episodes of the show become available for Prime Video subscription holders on November 25.

articles.title: Could Daniel Radcliffe And Emma Watson Join Harry Potter And The Cursed Child? Rupert Grint Weighs In
articles.summary: Could the original trio get back together?
articles.content:
Rupert Grint is the latest cast member from the Harry Potter films to join the Broadway run of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child , right on the heels of Tom Felton's successful run . With Ron Weasley in tow, he's already fielding questions about whether Emma Watson and Danielle Radcliffe could be next to join the stage play.

I'm sure the last thing Grint wanted to do was try to put the pressure on Radcliffe and Watson to say no, knowing the complicated thoughts both may have about returning. Daniel Radcliffe has been pretty adamant about refusing any opportunities to return , and Emma Watson has shied away from acting so much that there were rumors a few years back that she had retired .

It does feel like a good time, what with a new Harry Potter TV show on the way. The series' arrival on the 2026 TV schedule will likely spark even more interest than usual in the franchise, and possibly encourage a lot of millennials craving nostalgia to see Grint back as Ron.

It should be fun, especially given what Ron Weasley is up to in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child . He's running the joke shop Fred and George founded, while his wife Hermione is the literal Minister of Magic. As far as acting is concerned, it's more of a supportive role, but one that Rupert Grint will likely bring a special sparkle to.

articles.title: Ray Gunn's Brad Bird Reveals the Biggest Film Noir Influence on New Netflix Movie [EXCLUSIVE]
articles.summary: Brad Bird's Ray Gunn may look like something out of a 1930s science fiction magazine, but its titular detective owes quite a bit to Jack Nicholson. The director of The Iron Giant and The Incredibles is finally making the animated detective movie he's been trying to make for decades. While Bird drew inspiration from Humphrey […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Brad Bird's Ray Gunn may look like something out of a 1930s science fiction magazine, but its titular detective owes quite a bit to Jack Nicholson. The director of The Iron Giant and The Incredibles is finally making the animated detective movie he's been trying to make for decades . While Bird drew inspiration from Humphrey Bogart's detective movies, it was Jack Nicholson's performance in a 1970s neo-noir that helped shape the character of Ray Gunn.

Speaking exclusively with ComicBook's Chris Killian, Bird revealed that Roman Polanski's Chinatown was a big influence on the character of Ray Gunn. In particular, Bird loves what Nicholson was willing to do as an actor to sell the story of private detective J.J. Gittes. "In terms of character, I mean, for me, I love The Maltese Falcon and The Big Sleep with Bogart," Bird explained. "But to me, the best detective movie ever made is Chinatown ."

Bird singled out Nicholson's decision to spend much of Chinatown with a bandage on his nose. "He's snoopy and he's sticking the nose where it shouldn't be, and the nose actually pays the price," Bird explained. "And the lack of vanity he had of going through that movie with this just honking bandage on his nose is just… that's great filmmaking." While Nicholson informed the character, another Hollywood icon inspired his appearance. "Physically, we kind of looked at young Montgomery Clift," Bird revealed. "He kind of has striking eyebrows and a very interesting face."

Perhaps the most obvious comparison to Ray Gunn is Robert Zemeckis' Who Framed Roger Rabbit . Both movies take the classic private detective story and have some fun with the genre by populating their worlds with characters that could only exist through animation. In the case of Ray Gunn , it's aliens and robots rather than cartoon characters. Who Framed Roger Rabbit also got away with quite a bit for a PG-rated movie. Between the murder investigation at the center of the story and Jessica Rabbit 's relationship with her husband, there's plenty in the movie that plays differently for adults than it does for kids.

Bird has spent much of his career challenging the idea that animated movies are inherently children's entertainment. The Incredibles is as much a movie about a man going through a midlife crisis and struggling with his marriage as it is a superhero movie. And while Bird has yet to direct an R-rated animated feature, he told ComicBook that he'd be open to making one if the right story came along.

With Ray Gunn , Bird is getting the opportunity to make the kind of animated movie he rarely gets to see himself. Hopefully, its success will afford him and other filmmakers more opportunities to explore genres that Hollywood has largely reserved for live-action movies. If Bird does get to make an R-rated animated movie, let's hope it doesn't take another 30 years. Ray Gunn arrives in select theaters on December 4th and premieres on Netflix on December 18th.

articles.title: Buffy Once Made a Thanksgiving Episode That Was Much More Controversial Than Fans Remember
articles.summary: The late '90s were a pretty wonderful time to be a television fan. Friends was dominating Thursday nights, The X-Files was still making people afraid of perfectly ordinary forests, and every network seemed determined to find the next big supernatural hit. Meanwhile, Buffy the Vampire Slayer was busy proving that a show about a teenage […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The late '90s were a pretty wonderful time to be a television fan. Friends was dominating Thursday nights, The X-Files was still making people afraid of perfectly ordinary forests, and every network seemed determined to find the next big supernatural hit. Meanwhile, Buffy the Vampire Slayer was busy proving that a show about a teenage girl fighting vampires could be considerably smarter than its premise suggested. It also had a habit of making ordinary occasions extremely dangerous. Apparently, not even Thanksgiving was safe.

There's something particularly entertaining about revisiting holiday episodes from this era. They remind us of a time when television characters actually had to show up at somebody's house for dinner instead of sending a group text. But one of Buffy's holiday adventures deserves a closer look for reasons that have little to do with turkey or awkward family conversations. The fourth season tackled a particularly uncomfortable part of American history and wrapped it in a supernatural adventure. It wasn't exactly the sort of Thanksgiving special you'd expect between Home Improvement reruns and a football game.

That episode was " Pangs " from November 1999. Buffy wants to celebrate Thanksgiving with her friends, but a construction project awakens the spirit of a Chumash warrior named Hus. He's understandably furious about the treatment of his people and has no intention of quietly accepting the holiday festivities. Buffy suddenly finds herself dealing with an enemy whose anger comes from something considerably more complicated than an ordinary supernatural grudge. And that's where the episode gets interesting.

Here's a clip from the episode featuring Spike, a resident vampire, making a particularly blunt observation. It illustrates how the show didn't simply take one stance on American history but instead explored several conflicting perspectives. Looking back, that's one of the episode's greatest strengths. It encourages viewers to question the simplified version of history they've grown accustomed to hearing and consider the experiences of people who were often left out of the traditional narrative. Even decades later, there's value in using popular entertainment to introduce these uncomfortable conversations. Episodes like " Pangs " can remind us that understanding history means looking beyond the familiar stories and being willing to acknowledge perspectives that don't always make it into the textbooks.

The timing is worth remembering, too. America was preparing for Y2K, and Britney Spears was everywhere. The Blair Witch Project had turned a walk in the woods into a potential nightmare. Yet Buffy was tackling colonialism during a holiday that most television shows treated as an excuse for sitcom misunderstandings. Hus wants revenge for the violence committed against his people and Buffy has to stop him from killing innocent people. Meanwhile, Angel turns up unexpectedly and creates another headache for the Slayer. It's a strange combination of historical commentary and romantic complications. Somehow, the gang still has to figure out Thanksgiving dinner. Honestly, that's probably the most unrealistic part of the whole episode.

I've always found " Pangs " interesting because it understands that Thanksgiving comes with a rather complicated history. The episode doesn't simply give Buffy another monster to fight. It challenges the traditional story surrounding the holiday and brings Indigenous dispossession into a mainstream supernatural drama. That's a pretty ambitious move for a series that also gave us giant praying mantises and vampires with terrible fashion sense. The problem is that Hus becomes the villain of the week despite having legitimate reasons to be angry. Buffy ultimately has to defeat him to protect her friends. That creates an uncomfortable contradiction at the heart of the story.

There's also the question of how much room the episode gives Indigenous perspectives. The Chumash history provides the conflict but the story largely follows Buffy and her familiar circle of friends. That doesn't erase the episode's willingness to raise the subject. It does make its approach feel limited when revisiting it today. Still, I'd rather see a television series take an ambitious swing and leave viewers with something to discuss than watch another Thanksgiving special where everybody argues about who brought the wrong pie. " Pangs" doesn't get everything right. But it certainly gave Buffy fans something more interesting to remember than another holiday dinner gone wrong. And in Sunnydale, that's saying something.

articles.title: The Center of the News Universe Has Shifted to CNBC
articles.summary: The most consequential stories of this moment in time are happening on the Versant brand, from the stunning fall and rise of Nvidia's Jensen Huang, to Anthropic's IPO.
articles.content:
On Monday morning, CNBC senior Washington correspondent Eamon Javers was driving in his car when the President of the United States called.

Javers pulled over to the side of the road, and within minutes he and President Trump were live on Squawk on the Street to talk about Nvidia 's shock decision to bring back CEO Jensen Huang. Trump was on the show for nearly an hour, revealing his central role in securing Huang's return.

In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter Monday afternoon, KC Sullivan, the president of CNBC, called this morning's coverage of Huang and Nvidia a "really special moment."

"The President was so generous with his time, but it was fun to see Eamon bring that in, and then to have [Jim] Cramer jump in, Sarah Eisen jump in, Carl Quintanilla jump in, David Faber jump in, and to be able to get all those different perspectives, I just think it made such a rich discussion," Sullivan said. "I was really just so proud of the team and how they delivered."

For months, the news business has been focused on the 2026 midterm elections, and for good reason. But the midterms are over, and suddenly it seems the most consequential stories of this moment in time are happening on CNBC.

Nvidia stock soared 31.8 percent on Monday after the news, and the entire stock market rallied. Huang and Nvidia are not only a business story, they are an economic story, a political story, a national security story. It's a story of our time. For CNBC, it was also the second highest hour of web traffic this year, behind only SpaceX's IPO in June.

"In the world of media now, it's those who are essential to their audience and really understand their brand promise and deliver on that are the ones that are going to going to thrive," Sullivan says. "I do think that there's a lot of attention on the business world right now, and I don't think there's anybody who can compete with us in that arena."

For CNBC, that audience includes Trump, as well as seemingly every CEO of note in America. "I want to congratulate you guys. You covered it really well," Trump told the Squawk on the Street hosts during his marathon interview.

Huang, of course, is just the latest news. Last week, it was Cramer's exclusive interview with Nvidia's interim Colette Kress as the company reported its first (and only?) earnings report without Huang at the helm. Two days later Andrew Ross Sorkin had an exclusive interview with Anthropic co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei as the AI company IPOd.

"It's not like those things just happen. Those are long-term, trusted relationships," Sullivan explains. Eamon has been working that relationship to the President for many months, which put him in a position to do that; Cramer's relationship and trust with Nvidia is what allowed him to get that first interview with Colette; [Joe] Kernen's got a really important, longstanding relationship with the Treasury Secretary so when he was playing a major role over the last two weeks, to be able to have him come on our air; Sorkin has the relationship into Anthropic. Those aren't gimmes. Those aren't just things that happen."

Those moments all delivered double-digit ratings increases for CNBC on linear TV, and secured millions of social views and engagements, where they were shared, analyzed and moved the markets.

"At CNBC we pride ourselves on this, but we're the place that the most influential people go to at the most important times and most important moments," Sullivan says. "I think what it comes down to is that our audience wants to understand what is changing, what does it mean, and what do they do with that information? And that's everything from the midterms to the AI trade. When they're trying to to figure out what's going on, they turn to us. And I think our guests know that as well."

The TV news business can be fickle. General interest brands like CNN and NBC News can benefit immensely when major global news is happening, but tend to be consistent on a day-to-day basis. More partisan-leaning cable news channels like MS NOW and Fox News can rise and fall with the outcome of elections, or how people on the right or left side of the spectrum are feeling.

In the case of CNBC, the news cycle today is simply in their wheelhouse, and it is poised to continue over time as OpenAI weighs its own IPO, and with investigations into Nvidia assuredly coming from Congress (MS NOW may benefit from those too).

The CNBC boom also comes at a good time for the news brand, which is set to launch a new direct-to-consumer offering in the coming months. Sullivan is coy on what that specific offering will entail, but he notes that it will lean into its brand attributes of trust, and the live exclusives that the channel has become known for, be it an exclusive interview with the Amodei siblings, or having the President on the phone for nearly an hour.

"I think that what you'll see when we roll out our direct-to-consumer product early next year is that we're doubling down on that to deliver for the audience where and how they want it, making CNBC more useful and making CNBC easier to interact with and more rich for the consumer where and how they want it, but all built off of the same tenets that you saw today or over the last few weeks."

articles.summary: Image Courtesy of A-1 Pictures It's been more than six years since Sword Art Online released its second season, and the next installment is going to be its anticipated feature-length movie. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It's been more than six years since Sword Art Online released its second season, and the next installment is going to be its anticipated feature-length movie. However, the movie will only be released in 2028, and fans in the U.S. will have to wait even longer for its global premiere. Based on the critically acclaimed light novel written by Reki Kawahara and illustrated by BUNBUN, Sword Art Online made its anime debut in 2012 and became a massive hit. Over the years, the anime has released three seasons, three theatrical movies, anime extras, and even spin-offs. The franchise is still standing stronger than ever as fans are eagerly awaiting updates on the upcoming movie, Sword Art Online Movie: Integral Domain .

It's too soon for the movie to share its full trailer and release dates, but fans already know it's going to be another banger. The movie will follow the original story concept written by series creator Reki Kawahara and is set after the Alicization arc. Although the wait for the anime's return is longer than ever, there are several exciting anime fans can watch in the meantime to fill the void. If you're looking for anime with similar vibes to this classic fantasy, we've got you covered.

If you aren't already familiar with Kawahara's other works, Accel World will be a great starting point. The creator has written a few light novels over the years, out of which three have already received anime adaptations. Accel World has the same video game world-building and the intense moments that fans of Sword Art Online will immediately fall in love with. Unfortunately, even though this anime was released in 2012, it never received the attention it deserved. The story centers around Haruyuki Arita, a middle school student who has always been bullied for his weight.

He finds solace in playing online games, but his life takes a drastic turn after he encounters the school's vice president of the student council, Kuroyukihime, who will surpass all his high scores. She also introduces him to Brain Burst, a program that not only allows its users to accelerate their brain waves, but it also functions as an augmented reality fighting game. Kuroyukihime requests his assistance to get to the top, something Haruyuki finds it difficult to refuse, especially after she helped him overcome the bullies that tormented him.

This underrated isekai never received enough popularity to return with a second season. Although there's no denying that the first season is an incredible journey regardless of the fact that there's no anime continuation. This is yet another survival game where a group of people has been thrown into a world of fantasy that they can't escape from. The survival anime follows a group of strangers who wake up in a mysterious fantasy world with no memories of their past lives.

Unlike the generic isekai shows where the reincarnated or transmigrated characters adapt to their new surroundings quickly, this anime doesn’t shy away from showing the brutal reality of being powerless and unprepared in a completely unknown world. It’s a story of survival as it follows ordinary people who have been thrust into a dangerous world where they must fight monsters for food and money. Their struggles are visceral and slow-paced, emphasizing the weight of every decision while the characters try their best to come out of this dangerous world alive.

This is the newest anime from the creator of Sword Art Online , and it premiered in November 2026. The anime is still ongoing, so you can easily catch up with the episodes in no time. While the series is fairly new, it wouldn't be an exaggeration to say it's easily one of the best anime of the year. It has a much darker tone than Kawahara's most popular work. Not to mention that instead of the characters being trapped in a video game, Devils' Crest blends the virtual reality into the real world, making the situation more horrifying than anything.

The story follows sixth-grade students Yuma Ashihara and his twin sister Sawa. While playing a brand-new virtual reality MMORPG, they realize that their world is being fused with the game. It doesn't take long for the situation to turn from bad to worse as death keeps lurking around every corner, causing chaos and confusion among others. What's worse is that someone Yuma personally knows undergoes a terrible metamorphosis and turns into one of the game's horrifying monsters.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime you’d like to recommend that shares similar vibes to  Sword Art Online ? Let us know in the comments below.
