articles.title: Marvel’s ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Won’t Screen for BAFTA, Golden Globes and Other Early Awards Groups to Guard Its Spoilers (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Earth's Mightiest Heroes will fight Doctor Doom in the latest Avengers installment, but they won't face the first wave of critics and major guilds on the awards calendar. Marvel Studios’ “Avengers: Doomsday” will not screen for awards voting bodies before its world premiere, Variety has learned exclusively, a move designed to protect its theatrical run […]
articles.content:
Earth's Mightiest Heroes will fight Doctor Doom in the latest Avengers installment, but they won't face the first wave of critics and major guilds on the awards calendar .

Marvel Studios ’ “ Avengers: Doomsday ” will not screen for awards voting bodies before its world premiere, Variety has learned exclusively, a move designed to protect its theatrical run by keeping the film’s closely guarded plot turns out of the spoiler ecosystem ahead of its Dec. 18 theatrical release. The film premieres Dec. 14 in Los Angeles, just four days before it opens nationwide. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Oscars: 38 Animated Movies, 104 International Films and 190 Documentaries Make the Eligibility Lists, Setting New Records Two Directors, One Oscar: Can Lord and Miller, Los Javis, Fielder and Oppenheim or the Esiri Brothers Break Through?

The strategy follows a well-worn playbook for event films of this scale, from “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” to “Spider-Man: No Way Home.” But protecting the surprises comes at a cost, with “Doomsday” set to sit out a long stretch of the precursor season as voting windows close before most awards voters have seen a frame. The biggest question is: What does that mean for the Oscars ?

The most consequential window belongs to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. Preliminary voting for the Oscar shortlists begins Monday, Dec. 7, and closes Dec. 11, with shortlists in 12 categories announced on Dec. 15, the day after the film’s premiere. Those categories are animated short film, casting, cinematography, documentary feature, documentary short, international feature, live action short, makeup and hairstyling, original score, original song, sound and visual effects. “Doomsday” could factor into as many as seven of them.

Visual effects is where “Doomsday” has the clearest path because of how that race is structured, and the studio’s previous successes in the category (i.e., “Guardians of the Galaxy,” “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever”). Before the official 10-film shortlist is announced Dec. 15, the field is narrowed to 20 semifinalists, a list the Academy does not make public, though Variety has reported it exclusively in past seasons . That list is expected to take shape in the coming days. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Under current Academy rules, the president appoints a chair to preside over an executive committee of active and life members of the Visual Effects Branch. That committee reviews a list of eligible films and, through a series of meetings, selects up to 20 for further consideration. Achievements are judged on “the contribution the visual effects make to the overall production” and “the human artistry and skill, fidelity and technical achievement with which the visual illusions are achieved.”

Crucially, the rules build in flexibility that limits the risk of a major spoiler leak. The executive committee “will request that producers provide opportunities to view their films through advance screenings,” and if a film isn’t available two weeks before the selection meeting, excerpts may be submitted instead. If suitable materials aren’t made available, the committee can deem the film ineligible.

It’s not clear whether Marvel Studios screened the full film for the committee or submitted excerpts. Nonetheless, Variety has confirmed that “Doomsday” was submitted to the relevant Academy branches for consideration, along with the materials required for shortlist eligibility.

In other words, a far smaller group viewing a controlled screening or a curated reel gives Marvel a way to stay in the VFX conversation without exposing its third act to hundreds of voters (The Visual Effects Branch is among the top five largest of the Academy). That matters for a studio that has landed visual effects nominations for “Avengers: Infinity War,” “Avengers: Endgame” and “Spider-Man: No Way Home” but is still searching for its first win in the category.

In Variety’s most recent Oscar predictions , “Avengers: Doomsday” is among the early projected five film visual effects nominees alongside “Dune: Part Three,” “Project Hail Mary” and “Wildwood.”

What remains unclear is whether voters in the other branches where “Doomsday” could compete, including cinematography, makeup and hairstyling, original score and sound, will see the full film before the Dec. 11 deadline.

The rest of the early calendar has tougher hurdles to overcome.

The first casualty already came on Nov. 23, when the Critics Choice Association’s Below the Line Committee announced its shortlists . “Doomsday” was not screened for the committee in time for deliberations, and neither was Sony Pictures’ “Jumanji: Open World.” With no member screenings before Critics Choice nominations are announced on Dec. 4, the film will not factor into that ballot either. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Across the pond, BAFTA reveals its full slate of eligible films on Tuesday, moved up from its original Thursday date. Films must be made available on the BAFTA viewing portal to nearly 14,000 members around the globe and “Doomsday” will not be on the platform, in part to protect its theatrical window, according to sources. That effectively removes the film from this year’s BAFTA longlist consideration. Round one of BAFTA voting runs from Dec. 4 to Jan. 4.

The Golden Globes are also off the table. Voting in the film categories opens Tuesday, and closes Dec. 4, the same day Critics Choice nominations are revealed. Without a screening, “Doomsday” will be absent from every category, most notably Cinematic and Box Office Achievement, which recognizes films that gross more than $150 million worldwide, a threshold the film is projected to clear with ease.

“Doomsday” will also bypass the New York Film Critics Circle, the National Board of Review, the Los Angeles Film Critics Association, the AFI Awards’ top 10 and the Casting Society of America’s Artios Awards.

Not every road outside the Academy is blocked.

Nomination voting for the Actor Awards, formerly the SAG Awards, runs from Dec. 14 to Jan. 3, and members of the nominating committee will have opportunities to see the film in theaters. That keeps the door mostly ajar for the stunt ensemble and for Robert Downey Jr., the Oscar winner for “Oppenheimer,” whose turn as Doctor Doom is the film’s biggest swing.

There is also precedent for a December blockbuster surviving this exact calendar. “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” held its world premiere on Dec. 14, 2015, opened Dec. 18 and went on to earn five Oscar nominations. “Spider-Man: No Way Home” premiered Dec. 13, 2021, opened four days later and landed a visual effects nomination.

Marvel recently dropped the final trailer , which arrives after “Avengers: Endgame Encore” lit up the box office with a No. 1 domestic debut of $26 million. The re-release of the 2019 blockbuster included four new scenes that tie into “Doomsday” and added $143 million globally, making “Endgame” the highest-grossing movie of all time. In the wake of the record-breaking “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” Disney and Marvel are expecting “Doomsday” to be another massive superhero hit. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“Doomsday” brings back Downey as the villainous Doctor Doom, who appears to be a variant of Tony Stark/Iron Man from another universe. The sprawling ensemble reaches across the MCU and beyond, with several characters from Fox’s “X-Men” films officially crossing over into the franchise’s main timeline.

Alongside Downey, Chris Evans returns as Steve Rogers/Captain America, joining Chris Hemsworth as Thor, Paul Rudd as Ant-Man, Letitia Wright as Black Panther, Sebastian Stan as the Winter Soldier, Tom Hiddleston as Loki and Simu Liu as Shang-Chi. The cast of “The Fantastic Four: First Steps” also returns, with Pedro Pascal as Mister Fantastic, Vanessa Kirby as the Invisible Woman, Joseph Quinn as the Human Torch and Ebon Moss-Bachrach as the Thing, reuniting to face their longtime nemesis. Florence Pugh reprises her role as Yelena Belova following her appearance in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” alongside her “Thunderbolts” co-stars David Harbour as Red Guardian, Lewis Pullman as Sentry, Wyatt Russell as U.S. Agent and Hannah John-Kamen as Ghost.

The film also marks a major crossover with Fox’s “X-Men” universe, bringing back Patrick Stewart as Professor Charles Xavier, Ian McKellen as Magneto, James Marsden as Cyclops, Kelsey Grammer as Beast, Rebecca Romijn as Mystique, Alan Cumming as Nightcrawler and Channing Tatum as Gambit.

articles.title: Where to Find GTA 6’s Portal to PS2-Era Vice City & What You Can Do There
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games One of the coolest Easter Eggs in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a newly discovered portal that transports you back to the series' past, with retro graphics, music, and characters to discover. For players who loved the PS2 era of GTA, such as GTA 3, GTA: San Andreas, Liberty City Stories and Vice City Stories, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the coolest Easter Eggs in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a newly discovered portal that transports you back to the series' past, with retro graphics, music, and characters to discover. For players who loved the PS2 era of GTA , such as GTA 3 , GTA: San Andreas , Liberty City Stories and Vice City Stories , this is a must-find secret that transforms Vice City into its older self. While not something that provides an achievement, trophy, or other sort of reward, this blast from the past is one of the oddest and more elusive parts of GTA 6 players are discovering just days after the game's launch.

Like many of the other hidden references in GTA 6 , you'll have to do some exploring to figure out where the PS2 Vice City portal is, and what you need to do to activate it. This Easter Egg is actually a call back to a famous cheat in 2002's GTA: Vice City called LIFE IS PASSING ME BY, a code that allowed players to speed up the in-game clock so that day/night cycles went by much faster. By spelling out this cheat again in GTA 6 at various locations on the map, players can get a blast from the past that goes back multiple PlayStation generations.

The first place where you can start spelling out the Vice City code is in a radio tower within the Key Lento area of GTA 6 's map, a place that either Jason or Lucia can climb up into. Once inside the Badger radio tower, you'll find a small Storage room with a series of substation buttons, a lever, and a TV that shows "Club Malibu" on it, mimicking the same font as GTA: Vice City for sharp-eyed fans. A LPL poster is also in this space, indicating the brand of substations you have to travel to across the map to input the cheat mentioned earlier.

By turning on the power switch in this radio tower, you'll be able to hear a sound effect from GTA: Vice City playing, indicating the start of this side adventure. From here, notice the poster showing a PlayStation 5 in the room, with a message that says "LOSE TRACK OF TIME." This is a clue, referencing the PS2 buttons used for the Vice City cheat — W, A, D, and a dot (.). You might notice that some of the LPL substations have switchboards with prompts like "Press W," "Press D," "Press A", or "Press ."By tracking these PS2 commands with the inputs on a PlayStation controller, we can translate that W means Triangle, D is Circle, A is Square, and L1 is the dot (.).

The first code for LIFE IS PASSING ME BY on PS2 is Circle, Circle, L1, Square, L1, Square, Square, Square, L1, Triangle, Circle, Triangle, indicating a 12 button code. This means that 12 substations need to be visited to spell out the code, with the combination being the pressing of D, D, Period, A, Period, A, A, A, Period, W, D, W in the correct sequence. For example, the second substation you visit should have the letters "iF" outside the building, and a "Press D" button inside to get that part of the code together.

If you're still confused, check out the table below, which should have the location of every LPL substation you need to visit, the button you should be pressing, and the part of the Vice City code you should be looking for outside the substation building:

Fast traveling through taxi services, character swapping, or public transportation will automatically reset this process, forcing you to start over with the first substation. As a result, don't start this process unless you have a fast car you're ready to use to drive all over Leonida, and be ready for this to take some time. Once you hit every button in the right order, you'll get a mysterious text message from an Unknown number, telling you to visit the T.H. Power Station (Reactor 2) between the hours of 7pm and 6am, to reveal the secret you've been wanting to see.

The text that says "U-235-REACTOR2 19-06" is directing you to the T.H. Power Station east of the Hamlet area in GTA 6 , which has a similar lever you used to power on each substation. Pulling this lever with the code from the above steps inputted correctly activates a portal, transporting you to a retro version of Vice City. The graphics here are incredibly similar to GTA: Vice City and GTA 3 , calling back to the PS2 games that helped launch the series into superstar status. Here, you can mingle around what seems to be an exclusive nightclub, which has some familiar faces.

Traveling through what could be the initially teased "Club Malibu," this place has plenty of people, but none more famous than Kent Paul, a main character from GTA: Vice City . This character also appears in GTA: San Andreas , and shows up here in this nightclub in GTA 6 if you head to the bar or upstairs in the area. Interacting with Kent Paul upstairs will trigger a cutscene where another portal appears, taking you back to the beautifully rendered world of GTA 6 fully intact. Doing this will also land you several rewards, including:

Basically, this long journey lets you dress up as GTA: Vice City 's protagonist Tommy Vercetti, who themselves is an homage to characters like Al Pacino's Scarface or Ray Liotta's Henry Hill from Goodfellas . As another bonus, Kent Paul is transported to the GTA 6 world, with actor Danny Dyer reprising his role. A quick phone call from Kent confirms this after you exit the portal, concluding one of the strangest, yet most interesting Easter Eggs players have found for GTA 6 .

articles.title: Marvel's Doomsday Countdown Just Got Bigger With Real-World MCU Locations Getting Upgraded
articles.summary: The countdown to Avengers: Doomsday is drawing ever shorter, and now, in celebration of the upcoming release, some incredible real-world pop-ups connected to the movie are getting fans even more excited. Earlier today, the final Doomsday trailer was released, and with it came a flood of reveals, including confirmation that Bucky and Steve will be […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The countdown to Avengers: Doomsday is drawing ever shorter, and now, in celebration of the upcoming release, some incredible real-world pop-ups connected to the movie are getting fans even more excited. Earlier today, the final Doomsday trailer was released, and with it came a flood of reveals, including confirmation that Bucky and Steve will be reunited , a new look at the return of the X-Men, proof that the fan theory that Steve is really Loki is wrong , and so much more. That alone, with less than one month to go, has boosted interest in the upcoming movie once again.

However, the exciting reveals aren't only taking place on screen. Rather, several real-world locations have been upgraded with myriad Doomsday connections, and the size and scale of them are indicative of just how massive this upcoming MCU installment will really be. Specifically, the Doomsday countdown has begun appearing on various new installations, with some unique twists on what's been done before. Check out glimpses of these new installations and more about them below.

Social media has been abuzz with the news that various real-world locations have begun to feature massive Doomsday countdowns with unique MCU designs, which have popped up in tandem with the new trailer release. Among those that have been photographed and shared online are a huge Shuri/Black Panther mask, which has reportedly appeared in Oakland, California, and a giant Gambit card, which has landed in New Orleans, Louisiana. Presumably, there are more (or there will be), but those are the ones currently making the rounds.

A Doomsday countdown and giant Shuri mask have appeared in Oakland pic.twitter.com/vKexLKhCcm

A massive Gambit card has appeared in New Orleans with the ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’ countdown. pic.twitter.com/PEFuAil6iG

So far, it seems this unique marketing strategy is working. In addition to the appearances getting plenty of attention online, fans are also responding positively to them in the comments. In response to the post showing Gambit's card, for example, one commenter wrote, "This is actually so f—ing cool holy," and another said, "Promotion on a whole level." It's the latter, in particular, that feels notable. While Avengers movies, of course, always receive plenty of attention and fanfare, Doomsday really does seem to be getting a different level of marketing and promotion. After all, while these new installations are cool, they are far from the first real-world appearance from the movie (for one, there has long been a massive Doctor Doom statue in Japan).

While this hopefully means that Marvel has high expectations for the movie, it also very likely reflects the reality that the movie performing well at the box office and with audiences is critically important. Since Avengers: Endgame , the MCU has seemed to struggle to find its footing, and even with the expectation being that the MCU will get a soft reboot after Avengers: Secret Wars , Doomsday will be a very important step in making sure the MCU has a smooth path forward. If the effort going into the marketing is any indication, though, then this movie is more than primed to be a hit.

articles.title: David Greaves Says 'Once Upon a Time in Harlem' Is "An Act of Resistance" Against Efforts to Erase Black History
articles.summary: When William Greaves died before completing his Harlem Renaissance documentary, his son David, who had helped to shoot it but had never directed a feature film of his own, stepped in to finish it: "I couldn't imagine anybody else doing it," he tells The Hollywood Reporter.
articles.content:
When the veteran newspaperman David Greaves told people about the film that his father, the legendary documentarian William Greaves , had been trying to complete for decades — the one built around footage of a 1972 reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries at Duke Ellington’s apartment — some asked him why anyone would want to watch a bunch of old people sitting around talking. He bit his tongue at the time, but recalled during an interview at the recent SCAD Savannah Film Festival , "I was thinking, 'Oh, yeah, watch this!' Because I knew what those old people were talking about , and how important it was." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Awards Chatter' Podcast Danny Boyle on 'Ink' and Murdoch, the 'Trainspotting' Toilet Scene and How 'Slumdog Millionaire' Almost Went Straight to Video SCAD Savannah Film Festival 'American Doctor' Director on Her Powerful Gaza Doc: "I Wanted to Do Something"

David Greaves has been proven correct by the tremendous reception of that documentary, a one-of-a-kind chronicle of a critical chapter in African-American history, which finally premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January, screened at the Cannes Film Festival in May back and was released by Neon in October under the title Once Upon a Time in Harlem . Sadly, William Greaves didn't live to see the film's completion — he died in 2014 — but his work was finished by his son, who had been a 26-year-old cameraman at the 1972 gathering, but had never directed a film before. "I couldn't imagine anybody else doing it, frankly," David explained during a post-screening Q&A at Savannah's Lucas Theatre. (He also was one of 10 directors of outstanding 2026 docs who appeared on the fest’s Doc to Watch Panel .)

The fact that it took more than a half-century for the film to come to fruition was largely the result of the perfectionist tendencies of William and his second wife, Louise, David's stepmother, who died in 2023. "They had continued shooting on through the decades," further tracing the history of the Harlem Renaissance, David reports. While he's sorry that his father and stepmother weren't able to see the enthusiastic response to the film from audiences of all ages and races, he also feels that it all happened for a reason: "I think that this film was made to come out now , at a very important time in American history, when [some in positions of power] want to erase Black history," he asserted. "This film is sort of an act of resistance against that."

TV uber-creator Chuck Lorre , Grey’s Anatomy EP Zoanne Clack and A Different World showrunner Felicia Pride are among those scheduled to take part in the two-day event, which is set for Dec. 7-8.

Rhys Marc Jones's “ Black Church Bay ,” a mystery thriller starring “Heartstopper” breakout Joe Locke and Tom Cullen (“Weekend”), has been bought by Strand Releasing for North America.

Jones' feature debut, “Black Church Bay” follows a man whose world unravels after a secret relationship ends in tragedy. The deal was negotiated by Strand Releasing’s Jon Gerrans and The Bureau Sales’ Clémentine Hugot. Strand is planning a summer 2027 theatrical release.

“We’re thrilled to be working with The Bureau Sales on this innovative thriller that confronts complicated issues of gay repression and Cullen and Locke’s performances are so beautifully directed by Jones and create a real suspenseful thriller that is satisfying,” said Marcus Hu, co-president of Strand Releasing.

“Black Church Bay” world premiered at Zurich and went to play at Busan and the BFI London Film Festival.

“The film is the culmination of my thematic obsessions – a mystery thriller exploring notions of acceptance, authenticity and repression; how it is often our contradictions that define who we are and what we become,” said Jones.

"Black Church Bay" was shot last year on location in Anglesey and produced by Alex Polunin of Scotland-based Ossian International and Tristan Goligher of London-based The Bureau.

Polunin, who previously produced Jones’ short films “Pale Saint” and “Father of the Bride,” developed the film from its inception. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“One of the things that’s most distinctive and unique about this idea is the way in which it combines Rhys’s thematic and formal interests as a filmmaker – specifically in exploring the queer experience in such a nuanced way, but also through the genre engine of a thriller,” Polunin said.

Goligher, meanwhile, pointed to Jones’ ability to build and sustain suspense while exploring morally complex characters.

“It’s really rare to see short films where a filmmaker can create – and sustain – tension in the way that he did. This script does the same thing,“ Goligher said. “We’ve had a lot of very positive messaging around the gay experience in recent years but it’s also not everyone’s experience. Rhys wrote a very specific story about a very specific person and their experience, and I have no doubt that chimes with many people in the UK and the world.”

“But watching someone deal with a moral dilemma – trying to wrestle with the question of should they, and can they, do the right thing at their own cost – that’s also a very universal dilemma,“ added Goligher.

articles.title: As Abbott Elementary Fans Hope For Janine And Gregory’s Engagement At Disneyland, I Have A Question
articles.summary: Let's talk about another Abbott couple?
articles.content:
For six seasons now, Abbott Elementary fans have faithfully watched the relationship between Janine Teagues (Quinta Brunson) and Gregory Eddie (Tyler James Williams) progress. The pair have gone from good friends to committed lovers over the past several years and, now, it seems we’re on the cusp of a proposal. Many viewers are hoping an engagement will come during the Disneyland-set 100th episode that’ll air amid the 2026 TV schedule . I’d love that as well, but I also have a question about two other characters.

Gregory and Janine are, of course, the core couple on Abbott , but plenty of other romantic relationships amongst characters have been highlighted as well. As we anticipate what lies ahead for Janine and Gregory, I can’t help but wonder what the future holds for Ava Coleman and O’Shon, who’ve been dating since Season 4. I’ve enjoyed seeing their relationship develop as well as the funny moments that have resulted from that. With that, it’s hard not to wonder what the long-term plan for them might look like.

Gregory first expressed interest in proposing to Janine at the end of Season 5, which was about two years after the two finally got together. Ava and O’Shon will be reaching that mark later in the sixth season and, while great TV couples have different timelines, I could see O’Shon popping the question soon. Plus, given how encouraging O’Shon has been amid Gregory’s attempts to propose, who’s to say the former doesn’t want that for himself sometime in the near future?

Of course, I’m not saying anyone needs to be jumping the broom by the end of this season. I just wouldn’t mind seeing one or two engagements by the time Abbott’s finale rolls around next spring. That may seem like a long shot for Ava and O’Shon right now, but I’m feeling very good about Janine and Gregory’s chances of hitting that milestone.

Gregory has been trying to orchestrate the right moment to present Janine with a ring. During the show’s latest episode, “Competition,” he attempted to land a reservation at a popular Italian restaurant, where he could propose. Ironically, that plan became moot once Abbott’s Step Team punched their ticket to Disneyland, and Janine informed her man that they’d serve as chaperones on the trip. So it now seems like a given that Gregory will attempt to propose while he and his lady are in “The Happiest Place On Earth.”

articles.title: Steven Spielberg's Western Officially Revealed, And 4 Other Oscar Winners Are Confirmed Too
articles.summary: After returning to science fiction with this year’s critically acclaimed Disclosure Day, Oscar-winning director Steven Spielberg’s next film will be his first Western. The legendary filmmaker is set to helm The Heart in Winter, an adaptation of the 2024 novel of the same name by Kevin Barry, and Spielberg is not the only big name […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google After returning to science fiction with this year’s critically acclaimed Disclosure Day , Oscar-winning director Steven Spielberg ’s next film will be his first Western. The legendary filmmaker is set to helm The Heart in Winter , an adaptation of the 2024 novel of the same name by Kevin Barry, and Spielberg is not the only big name attached to the Universal and Focus Features project. Paul Thomas Anderson, whose previous film One Battle After Another is the most recent winner of the Academy Award for Best Picture, is set to write The Heart in Winter ’s screenplay. In addition, Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley, and Mark Rylance, all of whom have themselves won Oscars, have been cast in principal roles.

Like the novel, The Heart in Winter is described as focusing on a pair of star-crossed lovers living in the American West, who will be played by Buckley and Murphy. Buckley won the Best Actress category at this year’s Oscars for her performance in Hamnet , which Spielberg was a producer on, while Murphy took home the Best Actor prize for his work in the leading role of Christopher Nolan’s 2023 biopic Oppenheimer . Rylance won Best Supporting Actor for his portrayal of a real life convicted spy in the 2015 historical drama Bridge of Spies , which Spielberg also directed.

Spielberg and Anderson have personally won three Oscars each, with many other films they’ve contributed to having received other awards and nominations. Spielberg has won Best Director twice, for 1993’s Schindler’s List and 1998’s Saving Private Ryan , the former of which also won Best Picture. Spielberg has frequently spoken of his admiration for many Western films and the influence the genre has had on his work, which is made apparent by references and homages in many of his projects, including the semi-autobiographical film The Fabelmans , which contains a fictionalized depiction of Spielberg’s own first meeting with director John Ford, played in the 2022 film by David Lynch.

In addition to finally venturing into the Western genre directly, Spielberg has emphasized that the prospect of working with Anderson, a close friend of his, influenced his decision to direct The Heart in Winter . The film is the first narrative feature Anderson has written for another filmmaker to direct, suggesting that he was similarly enthusiastic about working with Spielberg. Anderson also won the Oscar for Best Adapted Screenplay for One Battle After Another . The Heart in Winter is currently set for release on an unspecified date in 2028.

Are you excited for Spielberg's first Western? Discuss in the comments.

articles.title: 4 DC Cartoons That Deserve a A Reboot, Including a Forgotten Batman Series
articles.summary: While DC has had and continues to have a tumultuous history in live-action, the franchise has consistently thrived in animation. Throughout its history, there have been some amazing animated series, from Batman: The Animated Series (1992) and The Batman (2004) to Caped Crusader (2024) and Justice League Unlimited (2004). While most ended on their terms, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google While DC has had and continues to have a tumultuous history in live-action , the franchise has consistently thrived in animation. Throughout its history, there have been some amazing animated series, from Batman: The Animated Series (1992) and The Batman (2004) to Caped Crusader (2024) and Justice League Unlimited (2004). While most ended on their terms, some ended sooner than they deserved, whether through cancellation or being left in limbo.

These four DC cartoons are among those great series and definitely deserve to make a comeback. And while some of these series might be familiar, there's one one forgotten Batman series we can't help but mention.

One of the most beloved DC Comics animated shows to date, Teen Titans premiered in 2003 and ran until 2006. The series followed the titular superhero team, comprised of Robin (Scott Menville), Raven (Tara Strong), Cyborg (Khary Payton), Starfire (Hynden Walch), and Beast Boy (Greg Cipes). Led by Robin (Batman’s sidekick), the Teen Titans protected the West Coast metropolis of Jump City from crime, often of the supervillainous variety. Throughout the series, the teens would also experience the struggles that go along with adolescence. The series ran for five seasons totaling 65 episodes, plus the film Teen Titans: Trouble in Tokyo , which served as the series finale. Each season had a different overarching villain, often connected to a member of the team, such as Trigon (Kevin Michael Richardson) in season five, the evil father of Raven.

The exact reason Teen Titans came to an end remains unknown. Will Wheaton claimed that Warner Bros. executives didn't like the pitch for the sixth season. Story editor Rob Hoegee said it was Cartoon Network's decision and that it was known ahead of time that the series was ending. Two more explanations were proposed by writer and producer David Stack. He said it could have been because of toy licensing (Mattel had all Cartoon Network licenses but not the Teen Titans license) or a drop in ratings during the fifth season as a result of their darker fourth season. Whatever the reason, the series was fantastic and remains a beloved part of DC animation history. Fans and the series cast continue to push for a sixth season return, and one would be well deserved.

Green Lantern: The Animated Series aired on Cartoon Network from March 2012 to March 2013, following a one-hour preview in November 2011. The series followed Green Lanterns Hal Jordan (Josh Keaton) and Kilowog (Kevin Michael Richardson), Red Lantern-turned-Blue Lantern Razer (Jason Spisak), and Green Lantern artificial intelligence Aya (Grey DeLisle) as they fought the Red Lanterns and Manhunters (a very different kind from the one seen in Lanterns ). It was the first Green Lantern series, the first DC series animated completely in CGI, and the first CGI series to be developed by Bruce Timm. The series tapped deeply into the lore. It featured the origins of Mogo, the planet that becomes a Green Lantern, and introduced other colors of ring-bearers.

Despite positive audience reception and viewership, the series ran for just one season of 26 episodes before being cancelled by Cartoon Network. This was in response to the low sales of the toys released for the show, which were impacted by the 2011 Green Lantern movie. The two projects were released in close proximity to one another, causing toys for the film to still be in stores, and the poor performance and negative reviews for it caused the audience to not buy them. Then, when the toys for the series came out, they didn't sell well either, and some stores didn't even carry them because of the full stock that remained for the film merchandise. The fallout from the film hurt the series and led to its premature cancellation. The series maintains a strong fanbase to this day, however, with viewers thrilled when it was put up to watch for free on Tubi after multiple years without it streaming. If any DC animated series deserves a comeback, it is Green Lantern: The Animated Series .

One of the most forgotten Batman series, Beware the Batman aired for one season and 26 episodes, just like Green Lantern: The Animated Series . The series followed Bruce Wayne (Anthony Ruivivar) in his early years as Gotham's masked protector. Together with his former MI6 butler Alfred Pennyworth (JB Blanc), bodyguard/partner Tatsu Yamashiro/Katana (Sumalee Montano), and eventually Lt. James Gordon (Kurtwood Smith), he protected Gotham from his Rogues Gallery. The series was unable to utilize most of Batman's most iconic villains, so it had to rely on his less commonly used ones. It did so to great success, featuring fantastic versions of characters like Professor Pyg, Humpty Dumpty, and Anarky (who became the series' main antagonist). But it was able to use classic Rogues as well, like Killer Croc, Ra's Al Ghul, and an interesting new take on Deathstroke.

The series had a rough time on television, which hurt its viewership. It premiered in July 2013, but was pulled from the air just three months later without an explanation. In May, the series moved to Cartoon Network's Toonami block, airing in the early morning. The terrible scheduling caused Beware the Batman to have low viewership. The network called the series a financial failure and canceled it. The final seven episodes were aired as a marathon on September 28th, allowing the series to end properly, though on a cliffhanger that remains unresolved a decade later. While its CGI animation was on the bland side, the story and performances were fantastic. The series deserves a continuation and a proper resolution to its story.

1.) Young Justice (2010-2022) Young Justice began as a series focused on classic Justice League hero sidekicks Robin (Jesse McCartney), Kid Flash (Jason Spisak), and Aqualad (Khary Payton) as they teamed up with new heroes Superboy (Nolan North), Miss Martian (Danica McKellar), and Artemis (Stephanie Lemalin) as they formed a new covert team within the League. The series would change a lot over time, growing with the core cast and introducing many new young heroes into the mix. It started as a teen drama, but eventually evolved into a mature adult drama that could get pretty dark at times (especially in one particular episode of season four). The series was also canon-adjacent to Green Lantern: The Animated Series , and Razer (once again voiced by Jason Spisak) appeared and continued his story from the series.

Like Beware the Batman , Young Justice also had a difficult production history. The series ran for four seasons, totaling 98 episodes. The first two seasons aired on Cartoon Network from 2010 to 2013 before being cancelled due to low toy sales cutting funding from Mattel. There was strong fan support for the series, which ultimately resulted in a renewal for a third season in 2016 that was released in 2019 on the now-defunct DC Universe service. A fourth season was greenlit later that same year and was released on HBO Max from late 2021 to June 2022. Since then, the series has sat in limbo. It has never been cancelled or renewed. The fanbase for the series remains passionate and continues to campaign for its revival. James Gunn said his plans for the DCU were inspired by Young Justice and Justice League Unlimited , renewing hopes that the series could return. With his controversial departure as DC Studios co-CEO, the future of the series is even more uncertain. Young Justice was a fantastic series that ended on a cliffhanger, and it deserves to continue.

What DC animated series do you wish would return? Let us know down in the comments.

articles.title: PS1 Exclusive Game Stealth Released on PS5 and Switch 2 After 31 Years
articles.summary: A PS1 exclusive game from 1995 has been stealth-released on PS5 and Nintendo Switch 2 after 31 years. This is the game's first re-release and marks the first time it has ever been available on a Nintendo platform. To this end, Nintendo fans may have no familiarity with the new release, but they may know […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A PS1 exclusive game from 1995 has been stealth-released on PS5 and Nintendo Switch 2 after 31 years. This is the game's first re-release and marks the first time it has ever been available on a Nintendo platform. To this end, Nintendo fans may have no familiarity with the new release, but they may know the game's predecessor, which was notably an SNES exclusive. To go from a Nintendo exclusive to a PlayStation exclusive with a sequel is incredibly rare.

The new re-release comes from Japanese developer Hamster Corporation, which specializes in re-releasing niche games from yesteryear, often plucked from the catalogs of the NES, SNES, and PS1. Its latest re-release is The Firemen 2: Pete & Danny from developer Media Entertainment and publisher Human Entertainment, neither of which exists anymore. What makes this particular release even more particular is that it not only took the series from Nintendo to PlayStation exclusivity, but that the first game got a Western release, while the sequel did not. To this end, this is also the first time the game has been available outside of Japan.

Unfortunately, while the game has been released in the West, and is no longer trapped to a PS1 disc impossible to find, it has not been localized. It's not text- or dialogue-heavy, but you won't be getting the full experience if you don't know Japanese, and you may struggle to play it at all. Meanwhile, as you can see from the trailer below, the game doesn't quite hold up in 2026. If you don't have nostalgia for it or the first game, it's probably not going to be a worthwhile time travel back to 1995. Those who are interested, though, will find it available for $11.99. The eShop does not have user reviews, but the PS Store does, and on there, so far, it has a perfect score.

A 32-Bit PS1 Game From Yesteryear For those just learning about The Firemen 2, it is an action-adventure game where you play as Pete and Danny, two members of the New York City District D Fire Station, First Platoon, who must save people trapped in a burning super-tall amusement building.

That said, it's worth noting this isn't the original in its purest form. It is the original game, but some modern features are available to modern players. More precisely, customizable button layouts, rapid-fire settings, multiple save points, rewind functionality, adjustable screen layout options, and CRT filters have all been added with the port.

If this PS1 nostalgia does not tickle your fancy, or if you're on a tighter budget, a remaster of an entire PS1 trilogy is currently available for just $2.54 , which is less than $1 per game included.

articles.title: New Xbox Report Claims the Brand Has Considered Ditching One of Its Most Divisive Features With Project Helix
articles.summary: A new report tied to Xbox has claimed that the brand nearly chose to abandon one of its most divisive features with its upcoming Project Helix hardware. While the Xbox 360 is by far the most popular Xbox console in history, it also introduced something that many users are still frustrated by: paid multiplayer. Rather […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new report tied to Xbox has claimed that the brand nearly chose to abandon one of its most divisive features with its upcoming Project Helix hardware . While the Xbox 360 is by far the most popular Xbox console in history, it also introduced something that many users are still frustrated by: paid multiplayer. Rather than being able to play any online multiplayer title for free on Xbox consoles, users have to pay to subscribe to Xbox Game Pass, or what was previously Xbox Live Gold . And while paid subscriptions for multiplayer are still required on Xbox and PlayStation platforms alike, Xbox leadership is said to have considered finally doing away with it, but may have now reversed course.

According to Windows Central , previous Xbox leadership intended to finally get away from the need to subscribe to a membership in order to play multiplayer titles on Xbox hardware with Project Helix. This plan was said to be rooted in the fact that Project Helix is meant to blur the lines between Xbox consoles and PCs, as it will instead be a hybrid of the two. With PCs not requiring a need to subscribe to any sort of service to play multiplayer games, Xbox seemed to think that continuing to do so on Project Helix wouldn't make much sense. However, the report claims that this plan might no longer be the case.

Following the retirement of Phil Spencer earlier this year , newly appointed Xbox boss Asha Sharma is said to have overhauled some long-term strategies for the company. One such change is related to Project Helix, which is said to now be more of a console-first platform that can also play PC games rather than the inverse, which is reportedly how it was conceived at first. Because Project Helix is now going to be more in line with how past Xbox consoles were, it's reportedly much less likely that Microsoft would drop the need for paid subscriptions when it comes to multiplayer games.

On one hand, it's easy to see why Xbox wouldn't want to do away with this need for paywalled multiplayer, as it's a simple way for the company to continue generating revenue. On the other hand, if Xbox were to scrap such a requirement, it would give it a distinct leg up against PlayStation, which is its most direct competition. No matter what Xbox leadership ultimately decides, it will surely still have an uphill battle when it comes to selling Project Helix, as the next-gen platform is reportedly on track to cost as much as $2,000 whenever it does arrive .

What do you think about this potential for Xbox to finally make multiplayer games free for everyone? And if it doesn't do away with paywalled multiplayer, will you be upset? Be sure to let me know down in the comments section.

articles.title: Everyone Knows Ted Kord and Jaime Reyes, but the Original Blue Beetle Was a Whole Different Kind of Hero
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics The Blue Beetle is one of DC's most enduring legacies, with Jaime Reyes being the most popular and the previous Beetle, Ted Kord, standing as one of DC's most shocking deaths. Both of these heroes have made a serious name for themselves, and both helped make the Blue Beetle name something every DC fan has […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Blue Beetle is one of DC's most enduring legacies, with Jaime Reyes being the most popular and the previous Beetle, Ted Kord, standing as one of DC's most shocking deaths. Both of these heroes have made a serious name for themselves, and both helped make the Blue Beetle name something every DC fan has heard of. Sure, Blue Beetle isn't a household name like Batman or Wonder Woman, but he stands at the cusp of superhero stardom. Heck, he even starred in his own solo movie, which is as sure a sign that a hero has made it as any other.

However, Ted and Jaime aren't the only ones who've called themselves the Blue Beetle. In fact, there was actually a third hero who took up the name, creating the identity that both would go on to make famous. Daniel Garrett was the original Blue Beetle, and his origins are actually incredibly important to the modern interpretations of the hero, but he's also so much more. He's actually the missing link that connects the Blue Beetle to every facet of power in DC, and living proof that a good reinvention could be all a hero needs to break into the spotlight.

The original Blue Beetle was actually Dan Garret, appearing in the Fox Feature Syndicate. He was a normal man who was granted incredible strength and durability by a neighborhood pharmacist's special drug, Vitamin 2-X. Donning Dr. Franz's blue, bullet-proof chainmail, he became one of the earliest Mystery Men. This version was a typical fighting man for the period, even having a sidekick named Sparky, who was a clear Buck rip-off. There's not much interesting about this version of the character, but things really took a unique turn when the Blue Beetle was reimagined as Dan Garrett, with two Ts, for the Silver Age by Charlton Comics.

This Dan was an archeologist who uncovered a mystical blue scarab while working in Egypt. It granted him incredible abilities, such as increased strength and flight, and even provided his Blue Beetle costume. Eventually, he was killed in action fighting his roommate Ted Kord's evil uncle and his robot army. Dan passed his Scarab and mission of justice onto Ted, but the new Beetle found that the Scarab refused to work for him, and had to make do with his own physique and advanced technology. Dan's origin would be slightly tweaked again when DC finally acquired the rights to his character , with him instead being Ted's college professor and leaving a family who knew his secret identity.

However, that wasn't the end of Charlton's work with the Blue Beetle. The team working on him actually planned to restore Dan, revealing that both Garret and Garrett were actually the same man, a chosen warrior of unknown gods. He would constantly reincarnate in new lives set up for him to act as their vessel, fighting crime as an immortal warrior across the ages. The company would never be able to pursue this storyline, but it was published in Americomics #3, which gave us this look at this first attempt to consolidate the Blue Beetle's various origins. Although this is the only time it would be done exclusively for Dan, it was far from the last rework for the Blue Beetle.

The Blue Beetle, more than any other heroic legacy, shows just how effective a change in direction can be for capturing the audience's attention. The original was a drop in the bucket of similar heroes, with nothing to set him apart from the multitudes of other heroes who did the exact same things he did. First, he utilized experimental drugs, but later he would shift hard into the mystical angle. Ted was a step in a completely different direction, using high tech and no superpowers, aiming for more of a Batman-inspired role while still bringing his own style. Jaime, meanwhile, uses the Scarab, but its history was reworked to be alien in origin, giving him a high-tech battlesuit that could create any weapon he could imagine.

From drugs to magic to science to alien technology, the Blue Beetle has changed drastically with each incarnation, and it's inspiring. Creators have been trying to make the character work for generations, each team passing the torch to the next as they refined what worked and left behind what didn't. Ted captured far more of an audience than Dan, but when he became stale and was killed in dramatic fashion, Jaime emerged with his own distinct style that elevated the hero even more. Blue Beetle is a perfect showcase of DC's incredible dedication to heroic legacies , as the company is willing to do just about anything to make the hero work.

Blue Beetle has origins that touch on just about every source of origins in DC, and each one provided a unique take on a hero that kept growing more and more with every year. Each incarnation is radically different from the last, to the point where you'd think their only similarities are their names, but each pays so much homage to what came before. Every Blue Beetle has been instrumental in the character's growth, and every person who dons the blue understands and respects that. More than anyone else, the Blue Beetle is a hero who honors the past even as he forges his own path, and that is the perfect style for any legacy hero.

Which Blue Beetle is your favorite? I love Ted and Booster, but my heart definitely belongs to Jaime. Let us know your number one Beetle in the comments below!

Photo credit: Paramount+ Avatar: Seven Havens has a much different look to it than fans saw with the previous Avatar: The Last Airbender outings, and one of the producers behind it all has addressed why the series has been changed so much with its art style and animation techniques. Avatar: Seven Havens is a sort of clean break […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avatar: Seven Havens has a much different look to it than fans saw with the previous Avatar: The Last Airbender outings, and one of the producers behind it all has addressed why the series has been changed so much with its art style and animation techniques. Avatar: Seven Havens is a sort of clean break from the rest of the franchise as it takes place hundreds of years after the events of The Legend of Korra . And that comes with a drastic change in the way it's designed its world too.

Avatar: Seven Havens executive producer Ethan Spaulding recently took part in a Reddit AMA for the series, and had been asked by fans why it looks so different than from what was seen in the prior series with characters having larger eyes and different proportions. As Spaulding explained, this was due to Avatar: Seven Havens being imagined with a "more obvious anime style " as the team was going for a more fantasy based look for its world.

"With all of the Avatar properties there is always a change in look and style , Seven Havens was always imagined as having a more obvious anime style to its characters," Spaulding explained. "We were going for a more fantasy based look and it being a Post Cataclysmic world this aesthetic choice seemed a good fit." When it comes to the actual animation of the series, Spaulding noted that the team wanted to lean into the "limited" style seen in other anime releases with plans to save it for the bigger moments.

"The decision was to lean into ‘limited animation’ as anime does and have fuller animation when the scenes really called for it, and yes time and budget is always a consideration in a tv series," Spaulding revealed. For those fans questioning the series' fluidity, Spaulding also stated, "The animation keeps getting better and better as the series progresses." That has already been seen with episodes like the first season's final few, and that's likely going to be case with the bigger episodes coming in the future.

"The Bigger tentpole finale episodes do get a bigger budget and also it is natural as a new series progresses," Spaulding also revealed when asked if the bigger episodes do get a more sizable budget. The producer also noted that "the animation gets better and better as animators become more familiar with animating the designs." Avatar: Seven Havens has been in the works for the last few years, so it's likely that the series is going to get even bigger and better from here as Pavi heads into the other Havens .

One of the drawbacks of this first Avatar: Seven Havens was the lack of one on one fights compared to what was seen in other series, but that's likely going to change now that the other Havens are set to be revealed. Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 is going to be hitting Paramount+ next May, with Season 3 hitting in late 2027. The series will then come to an end with Season 4 , so there's all sorts of opportunity for big moments. But how are you feeling about Avatar: Seven Havens ' art style and animation so far? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Disneyland’s Fantasmic Once Again Went Up In Flames, And I’m Starting To Worry About The Show’s Future
articles.summary: This is not a good sign!
articles.content:
Disneyland live entertainment is few and far between as of late, which is a shame considering the Anaheim theme park used to boast some of the best shows. On November 21st, one of the last and most beloved nighttime shows, Fantasmic, went up in flames for the second time in three short years. With two incidents and Disney’s desire to cut back on live entertainment, I’m really starting to worry about the future of the show.

The fire reportedly broke out during Fantasmic’s second performance of the night shortly before the show’s finale. While the Mark Twain finale was able to go on, flames can be seen behind the boat on the small stage set up on Tom Saywer Island. Guests at the park were quick to pull out their phones and film the growing flames as the Mark Twain, full of classic Disney characters , made its way around the river. Take a look:

The last two minutes of the show were canceled, and guests were asked to vacate the viewing area while the fire department handled the blaze. Thankfully, the fire was small compared to the 2023 incident that turned the Maleficent dragon animatronic into a giant fireball and forever changed the show. There’s been no word on the extent of the damage this time around, but considering the show was back Sunday night it safe to assume that nothing was affected and no cast members were harmed, thankfully.

Two fiery incidents are definitely a cause for concern, and with Disneyland executives’ history of scaling back entertainment to cut costs, I can’t help but worry about the show’s fate. After all, Fantasmic boasts a large cast of incredible performers and several floating units. Plus water screens, projectors, and fireworks. I’m no expert, but I’m willing to bet it’s one of the most costly attractions at Disneyland. Not to mention, the show is still feeling the loss of the Maleficent Dragon, which makes the battle between Mickey and Maleficent lackluster.

articles.title: GTA 6 Is a Reminder That Open-World Games Should Give Players More Freedom to Complete Missions
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Rockstar Games There's a contradiction at the heart of many open-world games where developers spend years building enormous environments for players to explore anyway they please, only to suddenly become very particular about what they're allowed to do once a mission begins. Take a different route? Mission failed. Try an unexpected approach? Mission failed. Use a perfectly […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There's a contradiction at the heart of many open-world games where developers spend years building enormous environments for players to explore anyway they please, only to suddenly become very particular about what they're allowed to do once a mission begins. Take a different route? Mission failed. Try an unexpected approach? Mission failed. Use a perfectly reasonable tool that the game has used hours teaching you to use? Somehow, also mission failed. It's a frustrating disconnect, particularly when the whole appeal of an open-world game is supposed to be the freedom to make your own decisions.

For this reason, among others, Rockstar has spent a long time refining its approach to mission design. Grand Theft Auto IV is an encouraging step toward resolving that contradiction. The studio has made a conscious effort to accommodate different approaches instead of constantly pulling players back toward one prescribed solution. Allowing for player agency is one of the most powerful tools a developer has, and it's something the entire industry could stand to embrace more often.

Rockstar's approach to mission design has been controversial on the small scale for quite a long time now. Their open worlds encourage players to experiment with practically everything, but that freedom can disappear the moment a story mission begins. GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 are particularly familiar examples of this disconnect, with missions that often expect players to follow a very specific sequence of events. You might have an entire arsenal at your disposal, yet suddenly find yourself unable to use a particular weapon because the mission expects something else. Even wandering too far from the intended route can bring an abrupt end to an otherwise successful attempt. There's a difference between guiding players toward an objective and insisting they complete every step exactly as the developers imagined.

GTA 6 makes a welcome effort to loosen those restrictions, and that becomes apparent within the first few hours. Missions feel less concerned with keeping players on a predetermined path, giving them more room to improvise when things don't go according to plan. Whether you're approaching an objective from an unexpected direction or finding your own way out of a dangerous situation, the game is more willing to accommodate decisions that might once have resulted in an immediate mission failure. It doesn't mean every situation has countless possible solutions, but there's a greater sense that players are allowed to figure things out for themselves. That's a meaningful shift in how Rockstar approaches the relationship between its authored missions and the people playing them.

I particularly appreciate that this doesn't require Rockstar to abandon what makes its storytelling work. There are moments when a mission needs to deliver a specific sequence of events, and giving players complete control over every interaction would make that considerably harder to accomplish. There's a considerable amount of space between a completely scripted sequence and an experience with no creative direction. GTA 6 demonstrates that developers can preserve the moments they want players to experience without dictating every single step required to reach them.

The games that stick with us most are the ones that give us something to talk about afterward because of something we did, not something obviously pre-ordained. Maybe a carefully planned encounter went completely sideways, or an unexpected decision created a situation the developers somehow anticipated. Those moments can be far more memorable than a perfectly choreographed sequence because they belong to the player. When you are responsible for that insane sequence of events that somehow let to a success, that distinction makes an enormous difference in how we remember an experience.

This why player agency should always be an absolute priority for developers across practically every genre, even those built around relatively linear narratives. A tightly authored adventure doesn't need branching storylines or dozens of different endings to give players meaningful control. Sometimes it's enough to let someone approach a combat encounter with their preferred strategy instead of insisting they use a particular ability. Other times, it means allowing players to interact with an environment in ways that feel natural rather than arbitrarily restricting them because the designers only accounted for one solution. Those decisions might seem relatively minor during development, but they can completely change how someone experiences a game. More importantly, they give players ownership over the moments they're creating.

There's a reason people love sharing stories about the ridiculous things that happened during their playthroughs. Those experiences become personal in a way that a developer's carefully constructed set piece rarely can, even when that set piece is spectacular. I don't want every game to become an immersive sim, nor do I think developers should sacrifice their creative vision in pursuit of endless possibilities. But there's a difference between giving players a story to experience and giving them the tools to make that experience their own. GTA 6 is a strong step in the right direction, that those two things don't have to work against each other. I'd love to see more developers recognize just how much that freedom can add to their games.

Do you prefer open-ended missions that let you experiment, or more tightly scripted experiences designed around a specific vision? Feel free to scribe your thoughts in the comments below.
